messages:
june: Heads up — after last night's merge (r/3482) prod streaming p50 jumped ~90ms -> ~250ms and p95 spiked. We paused the rollout at 3am. Can eng-runtime take a look? :eyes:
sam: Thanks — can you paste the CI perf job and canary logs? is this the same regression we saw in staging?
liam: grabbing logs now. CI perf job `streams-latency` failed on serialization/streaming test: `sse_stream_worker_test` latency +160ms vs baseline. Staging showed similar but smaller.
ops-bot: Deploy r/3482 to prod started 2026-03-17T23:14Z, canary 10% passed health checks, then alert: streaming-latency > 200ms. Rollout paused.
maya: quick summary from local profiler: two things look off — kernel selection fell back to generic_cpu_kernel for ~20% of requests for short sequences, and KV cache hit-rate dropped from 82% -> 61% for streaming sessions that use tool-calls. Flamegraph shows wasted cycles in serialization path after tokenization.
liam: interesting — why would kernel selection change? no model swap in the release, right?
maya: PR changed op attribute `requires_fast_attention` default to `auto` (was explicit true for some fused ops). Our kernel selector treats `auto` conservatively and picked generic path for batch shapes that previously used fast kernel. Patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3482/files
liam: that explains some cpu regression but not the SSE buffering behavior (delayed first chunk). Any batching heuristic changes?
june: r/3482 also modified batching window from 8ms -> 25ms to improve amortization for API non-stream workloads. Looks like we forgot to exempt streaming SSE endpoints.
sam: aha. So streaming requests were waiting up to 25ms before flush -> increases end-to-end first-byte latency. Combined with extra serialization overhead from kernel fallback and KV misses = bad. Can we short-circuit batching for requests flagged streaming?
liam: yes. I prototyped a small hotfix: in batcher when header `x-streaming: true` is present, force `batch_window_ms = 1`. Patch snippet:
```
# runtime/batcher.py
if request.headers.get("x-streaming") == "true":
    batch_window_ms = 1  # prefer low latency for SSE
```
I can push to hotfix branch and roll to canary.
maya: also found KV cache key generation includes tool metadata header `x-toolcall` after the PR — previously we normalized tool metadata away. Now toolcalls set `x-toolcall: {name}` which changed the cache key for prefixes and caused miss storm. Short-term: strip `x-toolcall` when computing kv-cache key for streaming sessions.
june: put both fixes in a single rollback-hotfix? or revert the batching change entirely?
sam: revert r/3482 seems safer for quick rollback (it touches both defaults). But ops wants a smaller blast radius hotfix for canary.
rollout-bot: Revert candidate created #3489. Hotfix candidate created #3490. Canaries scheduled once approvals complete.
liam: I'll open #3490 with the `x-streaming` shortcut + kv key normalization. test plan: unit tests for cache key invariants, e2e streaming smoke in staging.
maya: added perf microbenchmark comparing kernel selector before/after — the `auto` fallback adds ~40-60µs per token for short sequences on A100. If we revert op default we regain that.
june: timeline? ops, can we get 10% canary asap on hotfix?
ops-bot: canary window created for #3490 once PR is green. CI perf job queued; ETA ~15m.
sam: good. After hotfix can we add a regression test to CI that runs a tiny SSE stream workload measuring first-byte latency < 30ms? If we don't guard streaming fast-paths they will keep regressing.
june: yes please. Also add a lint that warns when batching window default is changed without streaming exemption.
liam: noted. I'll add the test and lint to #3490.
maya: postmortem notes: - avoid changing defaults that affect kernel selector behavior - normalize headers used in cache keys - streaming feature flag to bypass batching window - add small perf CI for streaming first-byte latency.
june: thanks all. keep threads on this. cc @eng-sre for runbook updates. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Canary for #3490 rolled to 5% at 2026-03-18T00:07Z. Metrics: p50 streaming down to 110ms, p95 still elevated but trending down.
rollout-bot: If canary passes, automated rollout to 50% in 30m.
sam: great work. We'll follow up with a short postmortem after stable rollout.
